newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index ends down as funds seek H stocks.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends down as funds seek H stocks.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B shares ended a quiet Friday slightly lower, with many foreign investors diverting funds to Hong Kong-listed H shares, analysts said.
The B share index closed at 133.17 points, down 0.47 or 0.35 percent. B share turnover was HK$46 million, little changed from Thursday.
"The B share trading volume has been really light because many people are diverting funds to the more exciting H share market," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
H shares are offered by mainland Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong.
Beijing's crackdown in May on stock-related irregularities had dampened speculation, leading to lower turnover, analysts said.
"Speculative stock trading has calmed down since the hard drive," an analyst at China Securities Co said.
In the B share market, television tube maker Shijiazhuang Baoshi Electronic Co Ltd was the worst performer, sagging HK$0.10 or 4.50 percent to HK$2.12.
In the A share market, distillery Hunan Jiuguijiu 0799.SZ ended its debut at 30.49 yuan compared with the 8.0 yuan offer price.
Analysts said they expected the index to remain laggard in the short term while investors remained cautious over first-half reports of listed due to be published by August 30.
"The B shares are unlikely to make sharp rises or falls in the near future," the J&A analyst said.
The Chinese yuan-based A share index gained 4.51 points or 1.09 percent to 419.64 points on turnover of 7.7 billion yuan against Thursday's 6.8 billion yuan.
